prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Conroe, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1163; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, if that's okay. You can use the claim number.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving south on the main road in Conroe, heading toward the shopping center. It was in the afternoon, and traffic was slowing down ahead of a light.

Q: And what happened next?

A: The car in front of me stopped suddenly. I braked, but I couldn't stop in time, and I hit the back of it. Then I felt my neck and lower back snap forward and back.

Q: Did you have your seatbelt on?

A: Yes, I always do. The airbag didn't deploy, though.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?

A: I got out, but I was sore and I held onto the door for a minute. The other driver asked if I was okay, and I said I thought so.

Q: When did you first seek medical attention?

A: The next morning. My lower back was stiff and the pain went down my left hip. I went to urgent care and they diagnosed a back strain. They gave me muscle relaxers and told me to rest and do physical therapy.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: Yes, I've been out for about a week and I'm limited to light duties when I go back. I'm still doing the exercises they gave me.

Q: Did you have any injuries before this accident involving your back?

A: No, not that I can recall. I'd never had any real problems there.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Just that I want to get back to normal. I'm willing to provide my medical records whenever you need them.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
